name: Sarah M.
social_challenges: I get overwhelmed in large groups and find it hard to initiate conversations with new people. I usually just listen and observe.
goals: I'd love to make one or two genuine friends who understand me. I'm tired of surface-level small talk.
comfort_helpers: Knowing the schedule ahead of time helps a lot. Quiet spaces are essential.
anything_else: I'm high-masking and often exhausted by the end of the day, so evening slots work better for me than mornings.

name: Marcus T.
support_needs_description: I have some anxiety in new situations but can manage with preparation
social_challenges: New environments are really hard for me. I need to know what's expected before I walk in somewhere.
goals: Social confidence mostly. I want to be able to go places and not feel like I'm drowning.
comfort_helpers: A clear agenda before we start. Also knowing where the exit is. No judgment please.
anything_else: I was in a social skills group in college and it felt clinical. This sounds different. I'm cautiously optimistic.

name: Jamie R.
support_needs_description: My son is autistic and mostly non-speaking. He uses a tablet to communicate. He really wants friends but gets overwhelmed easily.
social_challenges: He's had bad experiences in typical youth groups. The unstructured nature of most social settings causes him to shut down.
goals: He just wants one friend he can connect with. He loves shared activities — building things, playing board games.
comfort_helpers: Sensory breaks are essential. He does best with visual schedules and calm environments.
anything_else: I'm his mom Lisa. He's 22 now and I've been searching for something like this for years. Please consider him.

name: Alex K.
social_challenges: I've been through burnout and am trying to re-enter social life slowly. Large groups are out but small interactions feel manageable.
goals: Mostly just getting back out there at my own pace. Maybe meeting 1-2 people I can grab coffee with occasionally.
comfort_helpers: Outdoor or quiet café settings feel safer than windowless rooms.
anything_else: Burnout recovery is real. I need gentle re-entry not a crash course.

name: Taylor D.
social_challenges: I can handle social situations fine but find most people aren't interested in the deep conversations I want. Small talk feels hollow.
goals: Looking for genuine friendship. Also open to dating eventually but not ready to focus on that.
comfort_helpers: I like having a shared activity to fall back on when conversation stalls.
anything_else: I've done the online friend thing and it's exhausting. In person is better. Looking forward to this.

name: Jordan P.
support_needs_description: Autistic, ADHD. I struggle with executive function and sometimes interrupt. Working on it.
social_challenges: I interrupt when I'm excited and then feel embarrassed. I also have trouble reading social cues sometimes.
goals: Make friends who don't mind my quirks. Practice conversation in a safe space.
comfort_helpers: Reminders about personal space and turn-taking help. I like games that give us something to focus on together.
anything_else: I'm only 19 so most programs are either for teenagers or older adults. Would love to meet people my age.

name: Chris L.
social_challenges: I'm very independent and have a full life but have lost connection with people after moving here. I miss having local friends.
goals: Mainly looking to expand my social circle locally. Maybe 1-2 new friends I can see monthly.
comfort_helpers: I adapt pretty well honestly, just prefer quieter settings.
anything_else: Late diagnosed autistic. Did a lot of masking for years. Looking for people I don't have to perform around.

name: Morgan W.
social_challenges: I have social anxiety that makes it hard to reach out first. Once I'm comfortable somewhere I'm fine.
goals: Building up confidence to be more social. Eventually maybe dating but not there yet.
comfort_helpers: It helps if someone initiates the first contact and there's a clear activity planned.
anything_else: I've been in therapy for years which helps but I need real practice in a safe setting.
